base.description: The branch pull requests target and each spec branches from.

branchPrefix.description: Prefix for generated branches, e.g. tagteam/.

conventionsPath.description: A repository document implementers and reviewers are told to read. Null when there is none.

models.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

effort.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

roster.description: Every lens a plan may assign to a spec.

default.description: Lenses applied to every spec unless that spec removes one. A Codex cross-review and the adversary run in addition, always.

verify.description: Commands proving a candidate works. Zero matching commands is reported as not-applicable and waits for a person rather than passing.

when.description: Empty globs and empty keywords mean the command always runs.

ciWaitSec.description: How long to wait for GitHub checks, counted from when a check first appears on the pull request. Still pending at the deadline counts as not-run, which waits for a person. Zero skips CI entirely.

ciStartWaitSec.description: How long to wait for a first check to appear on a pull request whose commit has a workflow that runs on pull requests, before stopping for a person. May be missing: a missing key means 120. Zero turns the start wait off.

redesignEscalation.description: Whether a redesign of a rewritten area runs the implementer at the `escalation` block's model and effort, whatever `escalation.after` says: `always` does, `never` does not, `ask` leaves it to the person each time. Has no effect while `escalation` is null. May be missing: a missing key behaves as `never`.

autoMerge.description: Accepted and has no effect: nothing reads it, in either value. A spec that merges straight into the base always waits for a person, and `planBranch` replaced this key as the setting that lets specs merge without waiting. It stays declared, and optional, so that a file carrying it is not refused for a setting that does nothing.

setup.description: Commands making a fresh worktree buildable, e.g. npm ci.

copyUntracked.description: Ignored files a build needs, e.g. .env.test. Each must be ignored at its destination or the copy is refused.

reviewExclude.description: Globs whose contents are summarised rather than included in the review diff — lock files, snapshots, generated code.

maxConcurrentCodex.description: How many Codex calls may run at once across this repository. The cap spans every ship running here rather than allowing this many per ship, so raise it if you ship several plans at the same time.

fixRounds.description: How many rounds of fixes a candidate may take before the spec stops for a person. Each round is followed by a full review panel.

ciRepairs.description: How many times a red pull request may be repaired. Each repair produces a new candidate that runs the whole review cycle again with a fresh fix budget.

carried.description: The most findings a plan may carry before the ship stops and asks a person. At least 1: turning carrying off is `carry`'s job, not a 0 here.

followUps.description: How many fix units the whole-plan check may build from the plan's carried findings. Zero builds none, and every carried finding still real goes into the plan pull request's body instead. These units are separate from the whole-plan fix units `ciRepairs` counts.

escalation.description: Raised settings for a ship cycle whose fix rounds have stalled. Null is the ordinary behaviour: every dispatch runs at `models` and `effort`.

after.description: How many fix rounds run at the ordinary settings before the raised ones take over. At least 1: the ordinary settings always get one fix round, and wanting the raised model from the first fix is already expressible by setting `models`/`effort` to it.

models.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

effort.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

plan.description: Settings for the whole of /tagteam:plan, replacing `models` and `effort` there. Null is the ordinary behaviour: every dispatch runs at `models` and `effort`.

models.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

effort.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

planBranch.description: When true, a plan of two or more specs collects its spec pull requests on a branch of its own, plan/<slug>, each merging into it without waiting once its checks are clean, and nothing from it reaches base until a person merges the plan's own pull request; false ships every spec straight to base, where each waits for a person's approval.

carry.description: When true, a spec on a plan branch whose fix rounds ran out with only findings eligible to carry merges into the plan branch, and those findings are recorded in the plan's ledger and disclosed under that spec's `## Risk` and in the plan's pull request. A blocking finding is never carried, and a spec shipped straight to base never carries. False stops the spec for a person, as before.

autoRedesign.description: When true, the first time in a review cycle that the same file keeps failing, the ship answers `redesign` without asking, which spends one more fix round. Any later time it asks a person, and `accept` is always a person's answer. False always asks.

versionFiles.description: The lines that carry this repository's version, each a repository-relative file and one place in it — a JSON Pointer into a JSON file, or a line pattern with exactly one capture group — where one file may appear more than once, and an empty list means a ship never makes a version increase.

roleModels.description: The model each role is dispatched at. `lead` is every reader and planner (reviewer, re-check, adversary, explorer, plan-drafter, plan-reviewer, spec-writer); `worker` is the implementer and the fixer; `codex` is the model every Codex call runs. Every site carrying a role triple $refs this one, so a role added here is a role added everywhere. Note that `validate-json.mjs` returns on a $ref: a keyword written beside one of those $refs is silently ignored, so anything extra a site needs belongs here instead. Codex model names are not enumerable, which is why `codex` is a non-empty string.

jobEffort.description: The thinking effort each job is dispatched at. A reader that only has to answer whether one fix landed (`recheck`) needs less than a reader looking for what is wrong (`reviewer`), which needs less than the one writing the code (`implementer`). `planner` covers the explorer, the plan-drafter, the plan-reviewer and the spec-writer; `adversary` covers both the plan adversary and the code adversary; `codex` covers every Codex call. Every site carrying an effort map $refs this one. The Codex ladder is its own inline list rather than a $ref to the Claude one, though the two now hold the same words: `$defs.claudeEffort` is the ladder Claude dispatches are checked against, and Codex's words are Codex's to change.
